text:
marta: Quick review: I built an accessibility-first variant of the compact compare strip above the heatmap. Focus was visual patterns for overlap (not just color), keyboard flows, and concise microcopy. Mock: https://files.redwood/accessible-strip.png

sam: Love the direction. Can you summarize the pattern choices?

marta: Sure. Patterns: base = solid fill, compare = diagonal hatch, overlap = cross-hatch (both orientations). Each has a 1px outline for contrast. Badges (sample rate) use an icon + numeric; tooltips expand to `Sample rate: 1 in 10 requests`.

jin: How does the cross-hatch behave at very small widths? Might get noisy.

marta: Good call. For widths < 480px we switch to texture-less fills and rely on a tiny label (B / C) with `aria-labelledby` mapping to full description. Also we increase the outline weight to 2px so patterns aren't necessary.

lee: Keyboard spec looks solid. A few points: (1) left/right arrow moves focus between elements, (2) when a pinned range is focused, ctrl+arrow nudges by 1% and shift+arrow nudges by 5%, (3) enter toggles pin, (4) space opens sample popover, (5) escape closes. Add `aria-live=\"polite\"` region that announces pinned stats when pinned/unpinned.

ada: For screen readers, prefer `role=group` for the strip and `role=button` + `aria-pressed` for pinned ranges. The sample badge should be `role=button` with `aria-haspopup=true` and `aria-expanded` toggled. Also include `aria-roledescription=\"time range comparator\"` on the container.

sam: Implementation concerns: the hatch SVGs might be expensive if we render many strips. Can we use CSS gradients for hatches? Lighter weight and easier to color-swap for high-contrast mode.

marta: Yep leaning CSS background-image gradients for diagonal hatches. For cross-hatch combine two gradients. Provide fallbacks for older browsers (solid fill).

jin: Analytics: track `compare_strip.action` with props: action (pin/unpin/nudge/hover/open_sample), base_range, compare_range, sample_rate, overlap_pct, accessibility_mode (true/false).

lee: A11y test plan: NVDA + Chrome, VoiceOver + Safari, and a keyboard-only pass. Also test with high-contrast OS theme and 200% zoom. Document failures in the PR.

ada: Copy micro-nits: the pill help text reads \"Pin ranges to compare p95 & throughput.\" Replace ampersand with `and` for screen readers: \"Pin ranges to compare p95 and throughput.\" Also change \"Double-click to clear\" to \"Double-click or press Esc to clear.\"

ci-bot: CI: branch `a11y/compare-strip` 1 status: 3/3 checks passed. Visual tests: `compare-strip-contrast` OK.

sam: I'll add the CSS gradient approach and a small util to toggle accessibility textures. Jin can hook analytics. Lee will run the a11y smoke. Ada to validate screen reader phrasing. Marta to update mocks and attach a focused screenshot.

marta: Thanks — I'll post the focused screenshot and the component README updates here when ready :sparkles:
